description_full: MGX Resources Limited, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the mining, processing, shipment, export, and sale of hematite iron ore in Australia and China. Its flagship project is the Koolan Island mine site located in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. The company is also involved in treasury management, mineral resources acquisition, and investment activities. The company was formerly known as Mount Gibson Iron Limited and changed its name to MGX Resources Limited in November 2025. The company was incorporated in 1996 and is based in West Perth, Australia.

financial_summary: MOUNT GIBSON IRON LTD is a small-cap basic materials business with a $415M market cap on $135M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding. Operating margins are expanding by +5.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 2% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $37M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, thin -13.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
